notes:
**Head alignment by scanning.** Settings > Printing > Head stitching has a new Head alignment… window: print an alignment target, scan it on a flatbed scanner (a PDF or image, 3x5 cards up to letter size), load the scan and Studio measures the pen overlaps, the horizontal offsets and the photocell distance, proposes the values and writes them to the print head — with a backup of the old values first. It remembers its recent scans and only changes a value when their average says so, checks that each change moved the print as expected, keeps its settings between sessions, and logs every run (the scan, the readings, the plan) under ProgramData\VpStudio\align-logs. A Purge… button in the same window purges all active pens piece after piece until you stop it, with its own length, position and resolution. Back up / Restore in the same place save the head's stitching to a file and put it back on another machine.

**Machine start mode.** Settings > Machine now has "Start the machine": *When Print is pressed* or *When the printer is ready*. When Print is pressed, everything before the feeder in the start sequence starts at once, so the vacuum spins up while the job gets ready; the feeder waits until the printer has its first piece.

**Aborting a print stops the machine normally.** Abort runs the stop sequence and hands the machine back to the panel, the same as the end of a run, instead of latching a halt. Halt in the machine block remains the emergency stop.

**XML data files.** Load database accepts XML: each repeating element in the file is a record and its elements and attributes are the fields (nested ones are named by their path, such as Address/City; repeated ones are numbered). The Load database dialog offers only the file types Studio reads, and any other type is refused instead of loading as junk.

**Fixes.** "Show what the printer gets" now says why when it cannot render a piece. Scanning an ink cartridge after switching pages no longer adds it to the supplies order. Studio opens centred on its screen, or maximized when it does not fit, instead of running off the right edge at 150 % scaling. Typing works in the alignment window's number boxes. Machine events are never handled twice after the controller restarts.
